1#main: The prohibition of moving the dead and bones from their place. In it are 7 seifim. One does not move the dead and bones — not from an honored grave to an honored grave, nor from a disgraceful grave to a disgraceful grave, nor from disgraceful to honored, and a fortiori from honored to disgraceful; but within one's own — even from honored to disgraceful is permitted, for a person anticipates resting beside his ancestors; and likewise to bury him in the Land of Israel is permitted; and if they placed him there on condition to move him, it is permitted in every case; and if it is not guarded in that grave so there is concern lest gentiles remove him or water enter, or it is a found grave — one must move him {Rama: (Some practice placing Eretz Yisrael earth in the grave) (Or Zarua) (and this custom has support) (Midrash Tanchuma parashat Vayechi)}.
2#main: One does not transport a dead person from a city that has cemeteries to another city except from outside the Land to the Land: {Rama: Or they transport him to the place of ancestral graves (so implied in Or Zarua); and if he commanded to transport him from place to place, or commanded to bury him in his house and not in the cemetery — they heed him (same there); and it is permitted to put lime on him to consume the flesh quickly and transport him where he commanded (Rashba siman 369).}
3#main: One does not gather bones — neither from the coffin nor from the grave — to this side to bury another dead there, nor for the needs of the place.
4#main: A place where the custom is to bury in deep pits (meaning: deep ditches — from "in the pit they shall not rise") without a coffin until the flesh decomposes and afterward they gather the bones and bury them in a coffin — permitted.
5#main: A coffin they lined — it is forbidden in benefit if of stone or pottery — break it; and of wood — burn it.
6#main: One who finds boards in the cemetery — he should not move them from their place.
7#main: It is forbidden to open the grave after the stone cover was sealed, even if the heirs urge to open it to check whether he brought two hairs.
